title: Towards Understanding the Dynamics of Low-Rank Adaptation
claim: A structured initialization preserves more of the signal than the common random one, which supports using it.
layout: Single panel, three violin plots left-to-right, jittered points overlaid
description: A single violin plot titled "Comparison of Energy Preservation". The y-axis is "Energy Preservation Ratio", running from 0.00 to 0.07, with dashed gridlines. The x-axis has three categories: ETF, Gaussian and Orthogonal. Each category has a translucent violin shape with a black box-and-whisker marker down its centre. Jittered scatter points are overlaid on each violin. ETF is red and sits highest, around 0.05. Gaussian is blue and sits in the middle, around 0.037. Orthogonal is green and sits lowest, around 0.018. The eye goes first to the red ETF violin at the top left, then follows the downward staircase across the other two. The ordering makes ETF look clearly best.
caption: Comparison of energy preservation across ETF, Gaussian
abstract:
Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) is a widely used parameter-efficient fine-tuning technique, and previous works have studied the update dynamics of LoRA, showing that updating via the low-rank matrix $\mathbf{A}$ can be viewed as a process within the compressed subspace spanned by $\mathbf{A}^{	op} \mathbf{A}$ of the gradient $
abla f\left(\mathbf{W} ight)$. However, few works analyze how the properties of the low-rank matrices affect the performance of LoRA, since existing methods heuristically initialize the low-rank matrices as Gaussian matrices. In this paper, we provide a theoretical understanding of the update dynamics of LoRA. We reveal that the update dynamics can be viewed as a process within the subspace spanned by $\mathbf{A}^{	op} (\mathbf{A} \mathbf{A}^{	op})^{\dagger} \mathbf{A}$, and prove that when the gradient $
abla f\left(\mathbf{W} ight)$ is unavailable, if $\mathbf{A}$ is an Equiangular Tight Frame (ETF), $\mathbf{A}^{	op} \mathbf{A}$ and $\mathbf{A}^{	op} (\mathbf{A} \mathbf{A}^{	op})^{\dagger} \mathbf{A}$ can preserve the maximum information from the gradient $
abla f\left(\mathbf{W} ight)$. Thus, initializing $\mathbf{A}$ as an ETF is the optimal solution for low-rank adaptation when the gradient $
abla f\left(\mathbf{W} ight)$ is unavailable. Furthermore, we establish the convergence of Low-Rank Adaptation with a rate of $\mathcal{O}\left( rac{1}{T}ight)$ when $\mathbf{A}$ is an ETF. Extensive experiments show that initializing the low-rank matrices as ETFs significantly outperforms the commonly used Gaussian initialization for existing primary LoRA variants.
